classes.name: Alegeri pentru Camera Deputaților
classes.finest_note: Published by polling station (secție de votare) since 2016 in the AEP's open data and on prezenta.roaep.ro, with postal votes from abroad counted apart; earlier years by county and locality on the AEP archive.
classes.note: Lower house, elected for four years (Constitution arts. 62–63). Closed-list PR in 43 constituencies (the 41 counties, Bucharest, and Romanians abroad), with a 5% threshold for parties and higher ones for alliances, and the D'Hondt method at the national stage (Law 208/2015). Organizations of national minorities that win no seat get one each if they reach 5% of the average votes per deputy (Constitution art. 62(2)). 1990 was the Assembly of Deputies of the Constituent Assembly; 2008 and 2012 used single-member colleges.

cadence.administered_by: Biroul Electoral Central and the Autoritatea Electorală Permanentă
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant seat passes to the next candidate on the same list in the same constituency (Law 208/2015); a seat with no candidate left stays vacant, and partial elections were held for single-member colleges in 2008–2016.

access.evidence: Polling-station results of the 2016 and 2020 elections (Chamber and Senate, with postal votes and the seats per constituency); the ro.aep pipeline reads them.

Mixed member system under Law 35/2008: single-member colleges (315 for the Chamber) within 43 constituencies including the one for Romanians abroad, with seats allocated proportionally.
Second election under Law 35/2008; compensatory seats raised the Chamber to 412.
Return to list PR under Law 208/2015: 43 constituencies (42 at home and one abroad) plus the national-minority organizations' seats, counted as one nationwide contest.

classes.note: Direct election for five years (four until the 2003 revision), at most two terms (Constitution arts. 81, 83). A candidate needs a majority of the voters on the permanent lists in the first round; otherwise the top two meet two weeks later and the one with more votes wins.

cadence.runoff_rule: Elected in the first round with a majority of the votes of the voters on the electoral lists; otherwise the two leading candidates meet in a second round two weeks later, and the one with more votes wins (Constitution art. 81).

classes.name: Referendum național
classes.note: Called by the President on matters of national interest after consulting Parliament (Constitution art. 90), held on a constitutional revision (art. 151), or on the removal of a suspended President (art. 95). classes.name: Alegeri pentru Marea Adunare Națională
classes.note: The unicameral Great National Assembly of the People's and Socialist Republic, elected in single-member districts on the single list of the Front (Popular Democratic Front, then Front of Socialist Unity and Democracy); several candidates per district only from 1975. The 1948 Assembly adopted the 1948 Constitution. Official results notices in the Buletinul Oficial.

access.evidence: Results notices of the central election commission in the Buletinul Oficial, national and by region or county; no machine-readable official return.

classes.name: Alegeri pentru consiliile populare
classes.note: Regional, district, county, town, and commune people's councils elected on single Front lists from 1950 until December 1989.
classes.disposition_reason: Only national summaries were printed in the Buletinul Oficial; returns by council survive only in county branches of the National Archives, with no official digital copy.

classes.name: Alegeri pentru Adunarea Deputaților și Senat (1859–1946)
classes.name_en: Parliamentary elections of the United Principalities and the Kingdom
classes.note: The elective assemblies of the United Principalities from 1859 and, under the Constitutions of 1866 and 1923, the Assembly of Deputies and the Senate, chosen by census colleges until 1918 and by universal male suffrage from 1919; parliament was dissolved in 1938. The Assembly of Deputies of 19 November 1946 (unicameral; the Senate was abolished in 1946) is the last election of the Kingdom. Results by county in the Monitorul Oficial and the parliamentary records.

access.evidence: Results by county and college in the Monitorul Oficial; no machine-readable official return.

dates.note: Elections from 1859 to 1937 (with the last one, of December 1937) are known to exist and are not yet listed.
Assembly of Deputies; the Senate had been abolished.

classes.name: Plebiscite și referendumuri istorice (1864–1986)
classes.note: The plebiscites of May 1864 (Cuza's Statute) and April 1866 (Prince Carol), of 24 February 1938 (the Constitution of Carol II), and of March 1941 (approval of Ion Antonescu's rule), and the referendum of 23 November 1986 on cutting military spending, held under the Socialist Republic.

access.evidence: Results in the Monitorul Oficial and the Buletinul Oficial, national and by county.

classes.name: Alegeri pentru consiliile județene și comunale (1864–1938)
classes.name_en: County and commune council elections of the Kingdom
classes.note: County and commune councils elected under the communal and county laws of 1864 and the administrative laws of 1925 and 1929, until the 1938 regime replaced them with appointed bodies.
classes.disposition_reason: No official consolidated record: results were announced locally and survive in county archives and local press, not in the national official gazette.

classes.name: Alegeri indirecte
classes.disposition_reason: Officers chosen by elected bodies, with no electorate voting: the Prime Minister and government by a vote of confidence in Parliament, the presidents of the chambers, Constitutional Court judges appointed by the chambers and the President, deputy mayors and county council vice presidents by their councils, county council presidents by their councils until 2004 and in 2016, and the 1992 county councils by an electoral college of local councillors. Prefects are appointed by the government.

classes.name: Puterea judecătorească
classes.disposition_reason: No judge, prosecutor, or police officer is elected by voters: judges are appointed by the President on the proposal of the Superior Council of Magistracy (Constitution art. 125), whose magistrate members are elected by the general assemblies of judges and prosecutors (art. 133), not by the public.

classes.name: Desemnarea candidaților
classes.disposition_reason: No state-run primaries: parties, alliances, and minority organizations choose their candidates by their own rules, and independents qualify by supporters' signatures (Law 208/2015; Law 370/2004).

classes.name: Alegeri neteritoriale
classes.disposition_reason: The national-minority seats are won in the Chamber of Deputies election, on the general ballot, and are counted in camera_deputatilor; there is no separate minority roll. Elections inside professional bodies, universities, and trade unions are run privately by those bodies.

classes.name: Organisme cu scop special
classes.disposition_reason: Romania has no publicly elected school, water, or other special-purpose boards: school boards, inter-community development associations, and agencies are appointed or formed by the local councils (Law 115/2015 and the Administrative Code).
